sections.heading: Title
sections.source_text: InfinityGAN tackles a deceptively simple question: can a generative model synthesize images of truly arbitrary size, even infinitely large, while training only on small patches and a single consumer GPU? Existing high-resolution GANs hit a wall because their compute, memory, and training data all scale with the output resolution. InfinityGAN breaks this coupling by disentangling an image into a global holistic appearance, local structure, and fine texture, and generating any region patch-by-patch from continuous coordinates. The result is seamless, globally consistent images at sizes never before attainable, with constant memory and parallelizable inference, unlocking new applications like spatial style fusion, multi-modal outpainting, and arbitrary-length image inbetweening.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.source_text: Modern generative models have made remarkable progress in resolution and detail, but every gain comes at a cost. Training time grows, model size balloons, and you need large-field-of-view training images that are hard to collect. Crucially, existing generators are locked to the resolution they were trained at. Push them to synthesize larger images and their compute and memory explode quadratically, while their global structure falls apart. The paper asks how to escape this coupling entirely and synthesize images of arbitrary, even infinite, size from finite-sized training data on modest hardware.

sections.heading: Motivation
sections.source_text: Why do existing models fail when asked to grow? The key insight is that generators like StyleGAN2 secretly depend on zero-padding at the image borders to encode position. During training the padding pattern is fixed, so the network memorizes it. But when you synthesize a larger image, the spatial size of features changes, the padding-derived position encoding shifts, and the center of the image no longer receives sensible positional information. The result is drastically repetitive, structurally broken content. To synthesize truly infinite images, we need positional information that is valid infinitely far from any border, and a generator that can produce patches independently yet seamlessly.

sections.heading: Contribution
sections.source_text: InfinityGAN makes several contributions. First, it reformulates image generation as disentangling a global holistic appearance, local structure, and fine texture, each modeled by a dedicated component. Second, it proposes a structure synthesizer built as a neural implicit function driven by continuous coordinates, so any sub-region can be queried directly. Third, it proposes a padding-free generator that removes all zero-padding, letting patches be synthesized independently yet combined seamlessly with consistent pixel values. Fourth, it introduces a scale-invariant FID metric to evaluate synthesis at sizes for which no real reference images exist. Finally, it demonstrates practical applications the design unlocks, from spatial style fusion to outpainting and inbetweening at arbitrary sizes.

sections.heading: Method
sections.source_text: InfinityGAN's generator has two modules. The structure synthesizer is a neural implicit function that takes a global latent vector representing the whole scene's appearance, a spatially-arranged local latent tensor for local variation, and a continuous coordinate grid, and outputs a structural latent for the requested region. Coordinates are encoded with sine and cosine functions horizontally to exploit landscape self-similarity, and a tanh function vertically to capture saturation from ground to sky, so the model can be queried infinitely far from the origin. The texture synthesizer is a fully-convolutional StyleGAN2 with all zero-padding removed; it takes the structural latent, the global style, and randomized noise to render the final patch. Because there is no padding and the implicit function is queried per location, patches at the same coordinate always produce identical pixels, so independently generated patches tile seamlessly into an arbitrarily large image at constant memory. Training uses adversarial, R1, path-length, a mode-seeking diversity loss, and an auxiliary vertical-coordinate regression loss.

sections.heading: Dataset / Benchmark
sections.source_text: The authors introduce Flickr-Landscape, a dataset of four hundred fifty thousand high-quality landscape images crawled from Flickr, to evaluate synthesis at extended sizes. For image outpainting experiments they use scenery subsets of Places365, with sixty-two thousand five hundred images, and Flickr-Scenery, with about fifty-four thousand images. All InfinityGAN models are trained on small one-hundred-and-one by one-hundred-and-one pixel patches cropped from one-hundred-and-ninety-seven pixel images, and remarkably, training and inference of any size are performed on a single GTX TITAN X GPU.

sections.heading: Key Result
sections.source_text: On the Flickr-Landscape benchmark, InfinityGAN maintains a steady quality slope as the output grows, while baselines drift far from realistic global structure. Beyond four-times extension it surpasses the strongest baseline, scoring a scale-invariant FID of sixty-one point four one at four-times versus seventy-nine point eight for StyleGAN2 with non-constant input, and one-twenty-one versus one-eighty-nine at eight-times. Critically, its memory stays constant regardless of output size, while StyleGAN2 runs out of memory at the sixteen-times setting. A user study with fifty computer-vision-literate participants found over ninety percent preferred InfinityGAN's results over every competing method.

sections.heading: Ablation Study
sections.source_text: The central ablation isolates where positional information comes from. Starting from StyleGAN2 with non-constant input, the authors strip out all zero-padding, creating a padding-free variant with no positional cues at all. As predicted, this model fails to generate reasonable image structures and degrades sharply across every FID setting, confirming that the original generator was leaning entirely on padding for position. When the proposed structure synthesizer is added back, position is now supplied properly through the coordinate-driven structural latent, and generation quality returns to a reasonable state. This directly validates the padding-free plus implicit-structure design.

sections.heading: Headline Numbers
sections.source_text: The headline numbers tell the story. Scale-invariant FID of sixty-one at four-times extension and one-twenty-one at eight-times, both beating the strongest baseline. Over ninety percent human preference across all comparisons. Up to seven-point-two-times faster inference through parallel batching, cutting eight-thousand-pixel-square synthesis from one-hundred-thirty-seven seconds to nineteen. And when paired with In&Out for outpainting, InfinityGAN drives FID down to nine on Places365 and fifteen on Flickr-Scenery, roughly halving the error of the previous best. All of this at constant memory, on a single consumer GPU.

sections.heading: Takeaway
sections.source_text: The takeaway is that infinite-pixel image synthesis becomes tractable once you stop tying generation to a fixed output resolution. By separating the global appearance, the local structure via a coordinate-driven implicit function, and the texture via a padding-free convolutional generator, InfinityGAN produces patches that are independent yet perfectly consistent, so they tile into images of any size at constant memory and can be generated in parallel. Beyond raw synthesis, this single framework naturally unlocks spatial style fusion, multi-modal outpainting, and arbitrary-length panoramas and inbetweening, all from a model trained on tiny patches on one consumer GPU.
